quality_assessment: Chapter provides good explanation of statistics output and use cases, but has some inaccuracies in the output format description and field naming. Missing important details about actual field names from implementation.

issues.description: Example output shows incorrect field labels that don't match actual ripgrep implementation
issues.current_content:
3 matches
2 matched lines
1 files contained matches
5 files searched
150 bytes printed
1500 bytes searched
0.025 seconds spent searching
0.001 seconds spent in main thread
issues.should_be:
3 matches
2 matched lines
1 files contained matches
5 files searched
150 bytes printed
1500 bytes searched
0.025000 seconds spent searching
0.001000 seconds total
issues.fix_suggestion: Update example output to match actual format from crates/core/main.rs:461-481. Note that the time fields use different labels: 'seconds spent searching' vs 'seconds total' (not 'main thread')

issues.description: Section refers to 'Seconds spent in main thread' but actual output says 'seconds total'
issues.current_content:
- **Seconds spent searching**: Actual search time across all threads
- **Seconds spent in main thread**: Wall-clock time for the entire operation
issues.should_be:
- **Seconds spent searching**: Actual search time across all threads
- **Seconds total**: Wall-clock time for the entire operation
issues.fix_suggestion: Update field name to match actual implementation

issues.description: Example uses incorrect field name 'seconds spent in main thread'
issues.current_content:
0.400 seconds spent searching  (4 threads × 0.1s each)
0.100 seconds spent in main thread  (wall-clock time)
issues.should_be:
0.400000 seconds spent searching  (4 threads × 0.1s each)
0.100000 seconds total  (wall-clock time)
issues.fix_suggestion: Correct field name and show actual 6-decimal precision used by ripgrep

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention that stats are written to stdout (not stderr as might be expected for diagnostic info)
issues.should_add: Add note that statistics are printed to stdout after all search results. While most diagnostic output goes to stderr, --stats output goes to stdout.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add subsection clarifying that stats go to stdout and appear after search results

issues.description: Section claims JSON stats are 'not currently supported directly' but they are fully supported
issues.current_content:
# Machine-readable statistics (not currently supported directly)
# Workaround: Parse stats from stderr
issues.should_be: Statistics ARE supported in JSON output via --json --stats
issues.fix_suggestion: Replace workaround example with actual JSON stats usage. Show --json --stats produces summary message with type: 'summary' containing stats object and elapsed_total

issues.description: Doesn't specify the exact time precision format (6 decimal places)
issues.should_add: Note that time values are formatted with 6 decimal place precision (e.g., 0.025000)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add detail about time formatting in the Performance Metrics section

issues.description: States 'Statistics are written to stderr, not stdout' which is incorrect
issues.current_content: - Statistics are written to stderr, not stdout
issues.should_be: - Statistics are written to stdout after search results
issues.fix_suggestion: Correct the output destination for stats

issues.description: Could mention that --stats with --quiet forces complete search even though quiet normally exits early
issues.should_add: Add note that combining --quiet and --stats forces ripgrep to search all files to collect complete statistics, even though --quiet alone would exit after first match
issues.fix_suggestion: Add to 'Combining with Other Options' section explaining interaction with --quiet

issues.description: Doesn't mention the actual Stats struct fields from implementation
issues.should_add: The implementation tracks: elapsed (Duration), searches (u64), searches_with_match (u64), bytes_searched (u64), bytes_printed (u64), matched_lines (u64), matches (u64)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add technical details section showing the actual data structure for advanced users

Good explanation of the difference between matches and matched lines
Excellent practical examples showing real-world usage patterns
Helpful interpretation guidance for understanding results
Comprehensive coverage of performance tips based on statistics
Examples cover important use cases like performance benchmarking and codebase analysis

Include note about stats appearing after search results in stdout
Show actual test output to verify examples
Add cross-references to Performance and JSON Output chapters

metadata.validation_focus: Check that --stats output format and interpretation are explained
